HopVarietyBase.description: Identifies a hop and carries what a recipe must know to calculate with it, which is why `alpha_acid` is required: bitterness cannot be derived without it. `VarietyInformation` extends it into a full catalogue record, and `HopAdditionType` extends it with an amount and a timing.

producer.description: The grower or company that supplied the hops.

product_id.description: The producer's catalogue or lot number for the hops.

origin.description: The country or region the hops were grown in.

year.description: The harvest year of the crop.

form.description: The physical form the hops are supplied in.

alpha_acid.description: The alpha acid content of the hop, as a percentage by weight. Alpha acids are the main source of bitterness.

beta_acid.description: The beta acid content of the hop, as a percentage by weight.

VarietyInformation.description: The full catalogue record for a hop variety: `HopVarietyBase` plus the properties a supplier publishes, such as oil content and substitutes. This is the form used in the `hop_varieties` list at the document root.

type.description: What the variety is typically used for, given its aroma and bittering character.

notes.description: Free text notes about the variety.

percent_lost.description: The percentage of hop alpha acid lost in six months of storage, also known as the Hop Stability Index.

substitutes.description: Other varieties that can be used in place of this one.

inventory.description: The quantity of the hop held in stock.

HopAdditionType.description: A hop as used in a recipe: `HopVarietyBase` plus how much and when. Catalogue detail belongs in a `VarietyInformation` record at the document root, not here.

timing.description: The timing object fully describes the timing of an addition with options for a basis on time, gravity, or pH at any process step.

amount.description: The quantity added: by mass for whole, pellet or powdered hops, or by volume for an extract.

IBUEstimateType.description: Stores the IBU formula used in a recipe and, when available, the resulting estimated bitterness. If the formula is modified in any way, e.g. to support whirlpool/flameout additions, then please use `Other` for transparency.

method.description: The formula the bitterness value was estimated with.

value.description: The estimated bitterness of the recipe.

IBUMethodType.description: The formula used to estimate bitterness.

OilContentType.description: The oil content of a hop variety, and related compounds. Each oil is a percentage of total oil, the amount of which is total_oil_ml_per_100g. cohumulone is a percentage of total alpha acids, and polyphenols and xanthohumol are percentages of hop weight.

total_oil_ml_per_100g.description: The total amount of oil, including hydrocarbons, esters, and terpene alcohols in units of ml of oil per 100g of hop mass.

humulene.description: Humulene, as a percentage of total hop oil.

caryophyllene.description: Caryophyllene, as a percentage of total hop oil.

cohumulone.description: Cohumulone, as a percentage of total alpha acids. Unlike the other members it is an alpha acid, not an oil.

myrcene.description: Myrcene, as a percentage of total hop oil.

farnesene.description: Farnesene, as a percentage of total hop oil.

geraniol.description: Geraniol, as a percentage of total hop oil.

b_pinene.description: Beta-pinene, as a percentage of total hop oil.

linalool.description: Linalool, as a percentage of total hop oil.

limonene.description: Limonene, as a percentage of total hop oil.

nerol.description: Nerol, as a percentage of total hop oil.

pinene.description: Alpha-pinene, as a percentage of total hop oil. Beta-pinene is recorded separately as b_pinene.

polyphenols.description: Polyphenols, as a percentage of hop weight. Unlike the oils, not measured relative to total oil.

xanthohumol.description: Xanthohumol, as a percentage of hop weight. Unlike the oils, not measured relative to total oil.

HopInventoryType.description: The quantity of a hop held in stock.

amount.description: The quantity held in stock: by mass for whole, pellet or powdered hops, or by volume for an extract.
